Two people pull on ropes to move a boat along a canal. The boat moves at a constant velocity. The vector diagram for the tension in the ropes is shown. Which vector is the drag acting on the boat?
image: A diagram shows a boat in a canal being pulled by two ropes from its front. The forces from the ropes are represented by two vectors in a separate diagram, showing tension vectors. Four possible drag vectors (A, B, C, D) are presented, originating from a common point. Vector A points left, B points right, C points diagonally down-right, D points diagonally up-right. Given the boat moves at constant velocity, the drag force must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the resultant of the tension forces. The tension forces are directed generally forward, so the drag force, which opposes motion, would be directed backward (left).
